items.label: CryptoQuant
items.text: R to @cryptoquant_com: 7. Build the chart Before alerting, render the picture. A QuickChart node plots: BTC price + Taker Delta 7HMA + every historical signal marker, with a star on the current bar. One glance tells you where you are and what the bot saw.

items.label: CryptoQuant
items.text: R to @cryptoquant_com: 6. Outlier? Yes / No Keep the logic simple: IF |z| > 2 → outlier detected, flag direction (buy/sell pressure) ELSE → no outlier This is your decision gate. 90% of the time, it does nothing, and that's exactly the point. Signals matter because they're rare.

items.label: CryptoQuant
items.text: R to @cryptoquant_com: 5. Z-Score The engine. A z-score tells you how extreme the current delta is vs recent history: z = (value − 30p mean) / 30p std z > +2 → unusually heavy buying z < −2 → unusually heavy selling in between → noise One variable, one threshold.

items.label: CryptoQuant
items.text: R to @cryptoquant_com: 4. Now the math. Calculate: Delta = Taker buy volume − taker sell volume One hour of delta is noise. So smooth it with a 7-period moving average. That filters the chop and surfaces the real trend in buy/sell pressure.

items.label: CryptoQuant
items.text: R to @cryptoquant_com: 3. Fetch BTC Price (in parallel) At the same time, pull hourly BTC price (Open, High, Low, Close, Volume). You'll need it later to plot the signal in context. Running it in parallel to the volume fetch keeps the workflow fast; both land before the next step.

items.label: CryptoQuant
items.text: R to @cryptoquant_com: 2. Fetch Taker Volume Pull hourly BTC taker buy & sell volume from CryptoQuant. This is aggressive order flow, which is market-buying vs market-selling. One call gives you both sides. The raw imbalance is where the signal lives.
